newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France pilots set week's go-slow from Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Air France pilots set week's go-slow from Saturday.

text.p: The main pilots' trade union at Air France said on Friday that it had called a week-long go-slow protest starting on Saturday.
The SNPL pilot's union said Air France chairman Christian Blanc appeared to have opted for strong-arm tactics rather than negotiation over pay scales.
The SNPL union has been holding out in pay talks despite concessions from other unions and said its new call for a go-slow would last from Saturday to Friday.
"The action risks causing numerous delays on all flights," said a statement from the union, adding that it regretted the inconvenience this would cause to passengers.

Air France said on Thursday it had returned to profit in the year to March 31 1997, its first profit since 1989, and also said strikes by flight crew unions earlier in May had cost it 200 million francs.
